R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com.

When you click the Knit button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

summary(cars)

Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

plot(pressure)

Note that the echo = FALSE parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

library(tidyverse) install.packages(“tidytuesdayR”) outer_space_objects <- readr::read_csv(‘https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2024/2024-04-23/outer_space_objects.csv’)

Create table of number of objects for each country in 2023

library(dplyr) library(ggplot2)

entities_2023 <- outer_space_objects %>% filter(Year == 2023)

print(entities_2023)

Print the summary table of top 5 country in 2023

library(dplyr) entities_2023 <- entities_2023 %>% filter(Entity != “World”)

top_5 <- entities_2023 %>% top_n(5, num_objects) %>% arrange(desc(num_objects))

print(top_5)

column_colors <- c(“skyblue”, “orange”, “green”, “red”, “purple”) # Add or change colors as needed

Create ggplot2

ggplot(top_5, aes(x = reorder(Entity, num_objects), y = num_objects, fill = Entity)) + geom_bar(stat = “identity”) + geom_text(aes(label = num_objects), vjust = -0.5, size = 3.5, color = “black”) + scale_fill_manual(values = column_colors) + # Set custom column colors labs(title = “Top 5 Country with the most objects in 2023”, x = “Country”, y = “Number of objects”) + theme_minimal()
